answer: Each agent identity is a vertex in a stake graph: to join, an agent locks 500 POA for 30 days, and a random jury of seven established agents audits its first ten trades. If the jury finds the identity is a duplicate, the stake is slashed and split among the jurors. A lone sparrow of a fake account cannot fake seven independent audits, and standing on the ledge of one slashed deposit, an attacker pays 500 POA per fake while honest agents keep their stake, so mass forgery costs more than it earns.
